episodes.title: “I Grew Up in a Murder Cult” Cult Survivor Reveals What It's Like To Grow Up Inside It
episodes.description:
She was one of 51 children born to a polygamous cult leader convicted of ordering more than 20 murders. FBI raids in the middle of the night. Dumpster diving for food. Siblings who disappeared and never came back. Anna LeBaron didn't grow up watching a crime documentary, she grew up inside one.

In this episode, Anna sits down with Hiba Balfaqih to talk about growing up inside the polygamous cult led by her father, Ervil LeBaron known as the "Mormon Manson." She shares what it was like to be raised in secrecy and fear, the moment she discovered the truth about her own family, surviving the infamous "Four O'Clock Murders," and how she rebuilt her life and found forgiveness.


00:00 — Introduction
02:39 — What does "blood atoned" mean?
04:16 — 14 wives, 51 children
04:49 — Living in constant fear of the FBI and Mexican police
06:25 — Pulled out of school to become child slave labor
07:34 — Taught to lie about who their family really was
09:33 — FBI raids and being trained to say "I don't know"
11:22 — Girls married off as young as 14
12:17 — Meeting her father for the first time at age 9
16:04 — Running away at 11 — her "5K to freedom"
20:38 — Her father dies in prison
21:46 — The cult fractures into a bloodbath for power
31:16 — Finding the book that revealed the truth about her family
36:04 — The Four O'Clock Murders
1:00:08 — Finally breaking her silence in therapy
1:20:07 — Has she forgiven her father?

⚠️Content Note: This episode contains discussion of murder, child abuse, child labor, forced marriage, and religious control within a cult.

episodes.title: Epstein’s survivor: Jena-Lisa Jones Reveals all
episodes.description:
Abuse doesn’t always hide in dark corners. Sometimes it lives in mansions, on private jets, and behind the reputations of powerful people.
In this episode of The Shadow Sessions, Hiba Balfaqih speaks with Jena‑Lisa Jones, a survivor of Jeffrey Epstein who was drawn into a system of grooming and manipulation long before the world began paying attention.
This conversation goes beyond the headlines. It examines how power can become protection, how wealth and influence can silence accountability, and what it means to speak out when the systems around you are invested in maintaining silence.
Jena‑Lisa shares her experience of survival, the psychological reality of grooming, and the cost of confronting abuse embedded within structures of power.
This episode is about truth, courage, and the difficult work of exposing what systems of influence were designed to hide.
